items.summary: Boeing has announced a cut in its 737 Max delivery target for this year, which raises concerns. items.title: JLR looks to narrow gap with BMW in India on local Defender assembly and price cuts of up to Rs 34 lakh
items.summary: Jaguar Land Rover is focusing on local assembly of the Land Rover Defender to increase its market presence. Despite being third in luxury car sales, JLR expects to close the gap with BMW through these changes. Amba anticipates a 20% increase in annual sales volume due to local assembly benefits.

items.title: Regional rural banks to set up cybersecurity centres, develop threat intel
items.summary: Regional rural banks are set to improve their cyber security through the establishment of cyber security operations centres. They will also develop capabilities for vulnerability assessments and incident response as part of the reform agenda. The Financial Stability and Development Council plans to enhance cyber security measures following previous ransomware attacks. New initiatives will include implementing enterprise data warehouse solutions for better data management and reporting.

items.title: GST registration gets easier as CBIC drops Udyam proof, sets seven-day limit for approvals
items.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs has issued clarifications regarding GST registration requirements for businesses. Companies will no longer need to provide Udyam certificates or face rejections due to unpaid bills. Registration applications must be processed within seven working days with Aadhaar authentication. Tax demands must include clear justifications and cannot be arbitrary. These changes aim to simplify compliance and reduce disputes in tax administration.

items.title: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra flags need for 'prudent borrowing' as states face fiscal management challenges
items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra urged states to improve spending quality, adopt prudent borrowing and strengthen cash management to ensure fiscal sustainability. He also called for wider use of digital platforms for lending and direct benefit transfers.

items.title: Railways to launch door-to-door parcel services
items.summary: Indian Railways plans to introduce a door-to-door parcel service using the Rail Parcel App in eight cities. Customers in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, and other cities can book pickups and deliveries. Logistics partners will manage first-mile and last-mile services, while the railways will transport parcels. Bookings can be made online, easing the logistics burden for customers. Refunds for cancellations will also be available under specific conditions.

items.title: Centre eases GST rules for post-sales discounts, no prior agreement needed from November 1
items.summary: The Centre eases GST rules on post-sales discounts from November 1, no longer requiring a prior agreement, which is expected to help FMCG and pharma companies and retailers.

items.title: Textile PLI scheme likely to be extended by four years with easier norms for MSMEs
items.summary: The government plans to extend the PLI scheme for textiles for four years with easier criteria. This initiative aims to increase participation from micro, small and medium enterprises. The scheme, initially approved in September 2021, supports large-scale manufacturing of textiles in India. Lowering minimum investment and turnover thresholds is targeted to enhance accessibility for more applicants. Previously approved applicants committed investments of around ₹41,500 crore, surpassing initial projections.

items.title: India to emerge as major exporter to China, ASEAN, get edge in US trade pact, says Piyush Goyal

The country is also working towards an Investment Protection Agreement with the European Union. Goyal indicated that discussions for preferential trade agreements are progressing with multiple countries and groups.
